b8_measured.source: SNO NC, as applied in arXiv:2312.12907

scintillator_pc.description: pseudocumene + PPO (Borexino): (3.307 +- 0.003) x 10^31 electrons per 100 t, arXiv:1707.09279

heavy_water.description: D2O (SNO, 99.92 % isotopic purity, arXiv:1109.0763), M = 20.03 g/mol: per kt 2 x 10^9 / 20.03 x N_A = 6.014 x 10^31 deuterons and 3.007 x 10^32 electrons

scintillator_lab.description: linear alkylbenzene (JUNO): 3.38 x 10^32 electrons per kt, arXiv:2006.11760

Jiangmen.source: JUNO site; 22 deg N in arXiv:2006.11760 (sec. 2.1), 22.12 to the hundredth not yet checked

defaults.source: NuFIT 6.0, arXiv:2410.05380, table 1 (IC19 w/o SK-atm, NO)

nufit61_global.label: NuFIT 6.1 global (with JUNO)
nufit61_global.source: arXiv:2601.09791, eq. 3.1 (NuFIT 6.1 with the first JUNO data; the other parameters stay NuFIT 6.0's)

kamland_2013.label: KamLAND
kamland_2013.source: KamLAND, Phys. Rev. D 88, 033001 (2013), values as quoted in arXiv:2312.12907 fig. 47

sk_sno_2024.label: SK + SNO (2024)
sk_sno_2024.source: Super-Kamiokande, arXiv:2312.12907 (SK + SNO, independent of solar-model fluxes)

sk_day_night.description: Super-Kamiokande day-night asymmetry of the 8B elastic-scattering rate, all phases (5805 days), amplitude fit. SK convention A = (D - N) / ((D + N) / 2); SNUfish uses 2 (N - D) / (N + D) = -A.
sk_day_night.notes: the amplitude fit assumes the zenith shape of dm2_21 = 6.1e-5 eV^2; SK states similar conclusions hold over the region of interest
sk_day_night.source: Super-Kamiokande, arXiv:2312.12907, sec. VIII and summary

sk_sno_pee_quadratic.description: Daytime nu_e survival probability of 8B neutrinos from SK + SNO spectra, P_ee(E) = c0 + c1 (E - 10 MeV) + c2 (E - 10 MeV)^2, E the neutrino energy in MeV.

borexino_rates.description: Borexino pp, pep and 7Be interaction rates (counts per day per 100 t), with the inverse covariance used by Super-Kamiokande.
borexino_rates.source: Borexino (Nature 562, 505 (2018)), as used in arXiv:2312.12907 sec. VII D

sno_cc_nc.description: SNO salt phase (391 live days), energy-unconstrained fit: the ratio of the CC to the NC 8B flux, i.e. the CC rate above the threshold over the CC rate without oscillations for the measured total flux.

sk4_events.description: Super-K IV, 2970 days: solar neutrino (8B + hep) ES events extracted in 3.49-19.49 MeV recoil kinetic energy, in the 22.5 kt fiducial volume, after its selection (fig. 28 efficiency).

sk4_final.label: Super-K IV final sample (fig. 28)
sk4_final.note: signal efficiency relative to 8B ES events triggered in the 22.5 kt fiducial volume, reconstructed recoil kinetic energy
sk4_final.method: marker positions read from the figure's vector PostScript in the arXiv source (096.eps, ROOT 5.28): exact to the figure's drawing precision, 0.08 % in efficiency; the axes calibrated on its tick marks (0 and 100 %, 4 and 18 MeV)

b23_mb22m.summary: B23 with the Magg et al. 2022 abundances (meteoritic scale); high metallicity, consistent with helioseismology and the Borexino CNO rate. NuFIT 6.0's reference model.

b23_mb22p.summary: B23 with the Magg et al. 2022 abundances (photospheric scale); pp-chain fluxes within 1 % of MB22m, CNO within 1 %.

b23_aag21.summary: B23 with the Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021 abundances; low metallicity. The other side of the open solar composition problem; disfavoured at about 2.5σ by the CNO fluxes, not excluded.

b23_gs98.summary: B23 physics with the 1998 Grevesse & Sauval abundances. Superseded as the high-metallicity reference by MB22 (similar Z/X); kept in B23 for continuity.

b23_agss09.summary: B23 physics with the 2009 Asplund et al. abundances, superseded by the same group's AAG21.

b23_c11.summary: B23 physics with the 2011 Caffau et al. abundances (intermediate metallicity), not revised since; the 3D NLTE determinations of MB22 and AAG21 supersede it.

b16_gs98.summary: B16 (2017) with GS98. Superseded by B23 (Solar Fusion III nuclear rates, new abundances); used by Borexino 2018 and Super-K 2024, so kept for their numbers.

b16_agss09met.summary: B16 (2017) with AGSS09met. Superseded by B23.

bs05_op.summary: BS05 (2005) with GS98 and OP opacities. Two generations old; SNOwGLoBES's built-in solar flux.

bs05_agsop.summary: BS05 (2005) with the AGS05 abundances. Two generations old.

nufit61_global.summary: Global fit including the first JUNO data; JUNO dominates θ12 and Δm²21.

juno_2025.summary: The most precise single measurement of Δm²21 and θ12 (reactor, 59 days).

solar_global_2024.summary: Solar data alone. Its Δm²21 sits about 1.5σ below the reactor value; comparing it with JUNO is physics (solar against reactor), not a choice of input.

sk_sno_2024.summary: Super-K and SNO alone, independent of the solar-model fluxes. Solar side of the solar–reactor comparison.

nufit60_global.summary: Global fit before JUNO (2024). Superseded by NuFIT 6.1.

kamland_2013.summary: KamLAND's final reactor result. Superseded by JUNO, more precise in both parameters after 59 days (Δm²21 ±0.12 against ±0.19, sin²θ12 ±0.009 against ±0.03).

solar_kamland_2024.summary: Solar + KamLAND combination; JUNO now dominates the reactor side of any global fit.

prem_crust1.summary: PREM under the Moho, the CRUST1.0 column of the detector's 1 × 1 degree cell above it (Laske et al. 2013): the continental crust the night neutrinos cross last, in place of PREM's ocean and average crust. Still radial: the crust where a chord enters the Earth and the 3D mantle are not included.

prem_full.summary: PREM with its full radial polynomials (Dziewonski & Anderson 1981), the standard reference Earth and B3's. Its top 24 km are an average crust ending in 3 km of ocean, which describes none of the continental sites: A_DN of ⁸B moves by −2 % (SURF) to +4 % (SNOLAB) with the local crust.

prem_four.summary: PREM polynomials of the four main regions, the mantle extended to the surface: no crust (3.8 g/cm³ under the detector). A_DN of ⁸B comes out about 40 % above prem_full at Kamioka and SURF: the missing crust, not an Earth-model uncertainty.

prem_prob3.summary: Four shells of constant density (Prob3++), no crust. Solvable exactly by every code, which makes it B3's tool comparison; as a model of the Earth it is an approximation (A_DN of ⁸B about 20 % above prem_full).

bks.summary: O(α) electroweak and QED corrections of Bahcall, Kamionkowski & Sirlin (1995), the electron-recoil spectrum used by Super-K, SNO and Borexino.

snowglobes.summary: SNOwGLoBES's tables, Marciano & Parsa (2003), radiatively corrected total cross sections (applied as a ratio to the tree level at each threshold). An independent calculation of the same corrections.

tree.summary: Tree level, no radiative corrections. About 2 % above the corrected cross sections for ⁸B, 4 % at the highest recoil energies.

ar40_marley2_bhattacharya2009.summary: MARLEY 2 recommended model: HF-CRPA continuum and measured Gamow–Teller strengths from ⁴⁰Ar(p,n) (Bhattacharya 2009).

ar40_marley2_liu1998.summary: MARLEY 2 with the B(GT) from ⁴⁰Ti β decay (Liu 1998). Competes with the (p,n) strengths; the measurements disagree.

ar40_ksz2018.summary: Kostensalo, Suhonen & Zuber (2018): shell model for all transitions (sd-pf, multipoles to J = 3), quenched g_A = 1.00(5), ±13 %. Independent of MARLEY; folded over ⁸B it is 27–35 % below the MARLEY 2 calculations (with the free g_A = 1.27 the authors get 2.64 × 10⁻⁴² cm², inside the MARLEY 2 spread): the quenching of the Gamow–Teller strength is the open question.

ar40_marley2_bhattacharya1998.summary: MARLEY 2 with the B(GT) from ⁴⁰Ti β decay (Bhattacharya 1998). Competes with the (p,n) strengths.

ar40_marley1_bhattacharya2009.summary: MARLEY's v1 model (allowed approximation over all levels). Superseded by MARLEY 2's HF-CRPA continuum.

ar40_marley.summary: SNOwGLoBES's 2018 MARLEY table (allowed approximation), zero below 5 MeV. Superseded by MARLEY 2.

ar40_marley1.summary: SNOwGLoBES's 2018 MARLEY table with ⁴⁰Ti strengths, zero below 5 MeV. Superseded by MARLEY 2.

ar40_klmv.summary: Kolbe, Langanke, Martínez-Pinedo & Vogel (2003), RPA. Predates the measured Gamow–Teller strengths that dominate at solar energies.

default.summary: SNOwGLoBES's default table (Gil-Botella & Rubbia 2004 / KLMV 2003 era). Predates the measured Gamow–Teller strengths.
Kolbe, Langanke & Vogel (2002), as tabulated by SNOwGLoBES. The only ¹⁶O model here, so no range can be given.
Nakamura et al. (2002), AV18 potential, ±1 %; the effective-field-theory calculation of Butler, Chen & Kong agrees to about 1 %.

SNOwGLoBES's NC table (xs_nc_nue_Ar40.dat, 2018): QRPA by Pirinen & Suhonen, private communication, unpublished, without the measured ⁴⁰Ar levels. Here so that the NC column of SNOwGLoBES rate tables can be reproduced; not validated, and no other calculation to compare with.
